mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.1%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% over three months signals a tightening labor market, increasing consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.0% in the last 3 months
failure_condition: When UNRATE is below 4.0% for 3 consecutive months, SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent decline in housing starts (HOUST) and rise in real consumption (RSAFS) indicates a healthy economic pivot from housing to services, supporting positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST decline > 0.5% and RSAFS rise > 0.3% in the last month
failure_condition: When HOUST declines >0.5% and RSAFS rises >0.3% in the last month, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of strong industrial production (INDPRO > 100) and tight labor market (UNRATE < 4.0%), the combination signals an overheating economy that triggers Fed tightening, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO > 100 and UNRATE < 4.0%, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising real personal consumption (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer spending, supporting corporate earnings and driving positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: When RSAFS increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained employment growth (PAYEMS > 149,000 thousand) signals a robust labor market, increasing consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS is above 149,000 thousand for 3 consecutive months, SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.1%) combined with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 2.5%) indicates an early monetary policy response, which typically leads to positive 60-day S&P 500 returns as the market prices in accommodative stance.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS < 0.1% and CPIAUCSL > 2.5%, SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of high housing starts (HOUST > 1700.0) with declining starts, the housing market correction signals broader economic weakness, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST > 1700.0 and HOUST is declining, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
